neighbours.label: ' in' after ' just' when the clause before it describes a precaution or preparation, so that 'case' is expected next, whatever word really follows (packs a spare, just in winter); 'just in' after a plain event or place stays low
fire: The hikers carried extra water, just in summer.
My father keeps a spare tire, just in time for a puncture.
She saved a little money, just in the event of a layoff.
Pack a warm hat just in January.
They bought a second generator, just in time for an outage.
The nurse keeps bandages nearby, just in the event of a fall.
Bring a raincoat along just in spring.
We backed up the files, just in time for a crash.
quiet: The hikers reached the lake just in time for lunch.
My father arrived at the station just in time.
She found a little money, only in the kitchen drawer.
It snows here just in January.
They caught the second train just in time to see the show.
The nurse works nearby, just in the old town.
The roses bloom here just in spring.
We finished the race just in time for the prizes.
